Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 45 (CyrusOne missing-address campaign): matched this rows own AUS3 site code, publicly referred to by the operator as Austin III in a 2016 press release, to a dedicated aggregator listing giving a specific street address.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne is a large scale data center provider headquartered in Dallas, Texas. In 2016 CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchanges original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly 130 million dollars, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15 year lease. In November 2021, KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately 15 billion dollar deal, taking the company private, and that acquisition closed in 2022. CyrusOne has operated as a privately held company since, a company level ownership fact this registry had not previously recorded with a citable source. This specific row, Austin Data Center III, corresponds to this operators own AUS3 site code, which this operators own 2016 press release referred to publicly as the Austin III Data Center. A datacenterHawk listing for AUS3, fetched fresh this session, gives 7100 Metropolis Drive, Austin, Texas as the facilitys dedicated street address, distinct from the neighboring AUS2 building at 7301 Metropolis Drive.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne Austin Data Center III has no confirmed individual power capacity recorded, only a note that the Austin campus as a whole publishes 19 MW of IT capacity.

CyrusOne operates this facility as a privately held company following its 2022 acquisition by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for approximately 15 billion dollars. The facility sits on Metropolis Drive in Travis County alongside a neighboring data center, both part of a multi-building campus. The company holds relevant security certifications including SSAE 16, HIPAA, and FISMA, indicating the facility serves regulated workloads.

The absence of a facility-specific power figure limits visibility into how much compute this building actually supports. The published 19 MW for the entire Austin campus does not tell whether this third building carries most of that load or a small fraction. For tracking the binding constraint of power on AI scaling, individual facility capacity matters more than campus totals.

The ownership shift to private equity in 2022 means this facility no longer reports performance data to public markets. The CME Group transaction history shows how critical individual data center locations can be for financial infrastructure, but provides no current detail on whether this Austin building serves similar mission-critical tenants or the types of workloads it now hosts.
